The Past Perfect Tense with After
You can use the Past Perfect tense to refer to events that happened earlier in time than other events in the past.

You can use the Past Perfect in clauses with after.
  • After we had eaten dessert, we went for a walk.

You can also use after + Simple Past in the time clause and Simple Past in the main clause:
  • After we ate dessert, we went for a walk.
 Because the meaning of after tells you which event happened first, it is not always necessary to use the Past Perfect here. Using the Simple Past is also correct.
You can use the Past Perfect similar to the Present Perfect.

The Present Perfect refers to an event that happened at an unspecified past time with a relevance to the present.
  • I have just had a baby and I'm still on maternity leave.
    (I am speaking from the present time referring to an event that happened at no specific past time, but with a relevance to now.)

In the same way, if you are talking in the past and referring to a previous past event with relevance, you can use the Past Perfect.
  • It was 2005. I had just had a baby and was still on maternity leave.
    (I am speaking about the past. I'm looking back at an event with relevance to another time in the past.)

You can use the Past Perfect if you want to tell a story of events from a time in the past.
  • Jennifer Lopez was a forty-six-year-old actress, singer and dancer. She had grown up in New York and had begun her career as a dancer. She had worked as a dancer on television shows and in music videos. She had acted in her first starring role in the movie "Selena".

You can also narrate a story in the Simple Past from a time in the present.
  • Jennifer Lopez is a forty-six-year-old actress, singer and dancer. She grew up in New York and began her career as a dancer. She worked as a dancer on television shows and in music videos. She acted in her first starring role in the movie "Selena".

While both narrations are grammatically correct, it is more common that narration in the Past Perfect does not continue for very long. Most times, the speaker switches or brings the story to a time in the present to continue the story with the Simple Past.
In addition, if you give the events of the story in the order that they happened, it is not necessary to use the Past Perfect. You can easily use the Simple Past instead.
After Maya Angelou had written "I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings", it made history in the literary world as the first African-American nonfiction bestseller.
After Malcolm X had been assassinated, Maya Angelou began working with Martin Luther King.
Time Clause: Order of Past Events
You can talk about the order of events in the past by using time clauses in your sentences.

You can use different conjunctions like after, before and when to form time clauses to give an order to the events you are speaking about. These time words signal which actions come first or second, so you have to think carefully about the order of the events you are relating.
The time clause can either come before or after the main clause. If the time clause comes first, remember to use a comma after it.

Civil rights activist and prolific writer Maya Angelou was born on April 24th, 1928, in St. Louis, Missouri.
After Maya Angelou had written I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings, it made history in the literary world as the first African-American nonfiction bestseller.
After her parents had divorced, Maya lived with her grandmother. She was a child of seven when she experienced a traumatic event, and she refused to speak again for five years. That's when she realized that words had immense power.
Maya was awarded a scholarship to study dance and drama in San Francisco. There she was exposed to new ideas and political activism.

Before she began her writing career, she was a singer and actor in Porgy and Bess. It was at this time that she began to compose lyrics and become passionate about writing.
After she had met and married Vusumzi Make, a civil rights activist, they moved to Cairo, Egypt where she was editor of The Arab Observer.

Soon after she returned to the US, she made a connection with Malcolm X and helped build the Organization of African-American Unity. After Malcolm X had been assassinated, Maya Angelou began working with Martin Luther King. After King had also been assassinated, Maya was overcome. She began writing to comfort her soul. She published over thirty works that include poetry and nonfiction before she died. At the end of her life, she had won many awards and honors for both her dedication to the  Civil Rights Movement and for her literary legacy.
